newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia almost completes spring sowing - agency.
newsitem.headline: Serbia almost completes spring sowing - agency.

text.p: Some 2.3 million hectares have been sown to crops in Serbia, bringing the spring campaign almost to an end, Yugoslav news agency Tanjug reported.
Serbia planned to sow 2.37 million hectares this spring.
"Over 1.4 million ha of the total area sown is under maize, which is slightly above the plan," the Serbian Chamber of Commerce was quoted as saying.
It said the planned 108,200 ha to be sown with food grains were exceeded by 37 percent.
Sugarbeet was sown on some 59,000 ha, only 59 percent of the area planned. Some 20,000 ha of sugarbeet had to be re-sown because of rains and frost in April, the chamber of commerce said.
Sunflower was sown on over 160,000 ha out of 200,000 ha targeted and soybean on over 60,000 ha of the 80,000 ha planned.
Vegetables were sown on 90 percent of the planned 250,000 ha. Fodder crops were also sown on 90 percent of the planned 182,000 ha.
Serbia plans to export $700 million worth of agricultural and food products in 1997, 40 percent more than in 1996.
